answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks combine game-theoretic multi-agent auditing with topological cut verifications. When suspicious nodes form a sparse cut in transaction graphs, randomly sampled auditors inspect their interaction pulse. The protocol acts like an analytical prism, dispersing traffic into verifiable spectral clusters. Faulty syndicates suffer stake slashing, carving out dishonest collusions like hollow channels through porous karst bedrock. This structure enforces a superlinear attacker cost scaling with $O(N^{1.5})$ relative to Sybil count.
